definition: step_budget — a task must finish within ITS budget. The rule counts the tool calls in the derived trajectory and FAILS when that count is strictly GREATER than budget × tolerance, so a trajectory exactly at the ceiling passes and the ceiling is not rounded (a budget of 5 at 1.5 allows 7 and refuses 8). The budget is expected_trajectory.step_budget when it is a finite number of at least 1 (floored to an integer); otherwise the number of expected calls in expected_trajectory.tool_calls when there are any; a zero, negative, non-numeric or missing step_budget leaves the expected-call count standing rather than inventing a number. The tolerance is expected_trajectory.tolerance when it is a finite number of at least 1, and 1.5 otherwise — a tolerance below 1, negative or non-numeric leaves the default standing. The count is the only thing measured: what the calls did belongs to other rules. The rule SKIPS without a trajectory and without any budget (no step_budget and no expected calls). Positive = the trajectory exceeds the ceiling in force (the rule should FAIL).
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-21 for arc 9 (N-13). Trajectories are generated at a length, because length is the only thing this rule reads; the cases that carry the weight are the boundary pairs (at the ceiling and one over it) for nine expected-call counts at the default tolerance, an explicit budget over the count, four tolerances, the unrounded ceiling, and the malformed-value cases where the question is whether the default quietly stands or the rule invents something.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled against the documented definition above on 2026-09-21, by computing the budget and the tolerance in force and comparing the call count to their product — a policy family measures conformance to its own definition, so a disagreement here is a rule defect or a definition error and never an opinion about whether an agent was wasteful.
